# B494 row (k): raw cosign signature fetch per transport, the digest cosign names, the format, and the Puller's index binding
confined: no (host process; the fetch is a plain net/http client, no ingest, no platform policy).
cosign: v3.1.3 (GitCommit 11926fa5bbbbde47e88fc006b625a17769b743b2), binary cosign-darwin-arm64 sha256
  5cf948c2f4dfe59687bdd0b8523709067383e03982cc543475c8a7dc70e92a76, equal to the release's cosign_checksums.txt line.
keys: throwaway (cosign generate-key-pair in scratch), signer SPKI sha256 0a7bf17a7496e5ebdacba15b71f247a78808edf977872622a3567ae7e7fe2b23.

## signing commands and the format each produced
legacy:  cosign sign --key cosign.key --tlog-upload=false --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false --allow-http-registry -y <ref>@<digest>
  -> a tag sha256-<hex>.sig in the image's repository; one OCI manifest layer, mediaType application/vnd.dev.cosign.simplesigning.v1+json,
     signature in the layer annotation dev.cosignproject.cosign/signature (base64 DER ECDSA over the payload bytes).
  cosign prints: 'Flag --new-bundle-format has been deprecated, this will be the only supported format in future versions'
default: cosign sign --key cosign.key --tlog-upload=false --use-signing-config=false --allow-http-registry -y <ref>@<digest>
  -> NO .sig tag; an OCI 1.1 referrer (artifactType application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json) whose layer is a sigstore
     bundle v0.3: a DSSE envelope, payloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json, predicateType https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1,
     subject = the manifest digest. cosign prints: 'Flag --tlog-upload has been deprecated, prefer using a --signing-config file'.
  (--tlog-upload, --new-bundle-format are hidden flags in v3.1.3's --help.)
So the lab's cosign defaults to the bundle/referrers form; the legacy .sig form needs deprecated flags.

## which digest the payload names
single-platform artifact b494/hello-wasm@sha256:4ed9ca42c7836b43d31be30a34160541cadcd84eddba2978f605d4869b63dfec:
  critical.image.docker-manifest-digest = sha256:4ed9ca42c7836b43d31be30a34160541cadcd84eddba2978f605d4869b63dfec (the manifest itself)
index b494/hello-wasm-index@sha256:976f8b3ed85d5605193a93a118f81c60501e8d65f6316e781c6d7f9d2ebbc95a (one child sha256:4ed9ca42...):
  critical.image.docker-manifest-digest = sha256:976f8b3ed85d5605193a93a118f81c60501e8d65f6316e781c6d7f9d2ebbc95a (the INDEX);
  the child carries no signature of its own (cell 'primary/index child' below: no .sig tag, empty referrers). cosign signs
  children only with --recursive.

## does the Puller keep the parent index digest for the resolved child? NO
apis ImageManifest declares index_digest = 101 ('the digest of the multi-platform INDEX the reference resolved through'):
  1175:  string index_digest = 101;
but nothing in runtimed or k3sm ever sets it (grep IndexDigest over pkg/ internal/ cmd/ and k3sm/pkg, non-test, non-pb):
  (no assignment; the only IndexDigest hits are the unrelated ErrIndexDigestMismatch sentinel)
PullResult.Descriptor is 'the resolved manifest's OWN content descriptor' (the child), and the FetchFunc seam returns a
ggcrv1.Image (the child) so the index is gone before ingest builds the result:
  76:type FetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, ref string, cred *RegistryCredential, policy PlatformPolicy) (ggcrv1.Image, error)
  77-
  78-// ErrInvalidReference is the decided verdict for an image reference that is not
  261:	// Descriptor is the resolved manifest's OWN content descriptor: media type,
Consequence: an index-signed image cannot be verified against PullResult today; a verifier needs the Puller to populate
index_digest (bound to the child) first, or must accept only a signature over the child digest.

## transports
primary   = a registry the node pulls from directly; here the scratch registry on this Mac (plain HTTP, LAN address).
mirror    = the peer-ingest mirror path (pkg/image/mirror.go): the server node's ingest registry at its advertised meshHost.
cluster   = the cluster-registry spelling (pkg/image/clusterregistry.go): the in-cluster Service DNS name, plain HTTP.
The mirror and cluster transports both reach the server node's ingest registry, which refuses a push without its per-boot
credential (401 below; the credential file is _k3sm-only and was not read, no sudo). So no artifact of this run can be placed
there and its 'mismatched digest' cell is N/A; its 'no signature' cells use an image already in that registry (repo 'probe').

## the table (outcome / raw status)
| transport | unreachable | no signature | mismatched digest |
|---|---|---|---|
| primary | 503 on /v2/ (a listener answering 5xx); and dial: connection refused | GET .../manifests/sha256-<hex>.sig 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN + referrers 200 with no sigstore entry | .sig 200, layer blob 200 and digest-verified, payload docker-manifest-digest sha256:4ed9ca42... != resolved sha256:8709190d... |
| mirror (peer ingest, mesh) | dial: connection refused (wrong port; an unrouted mesh address also refused) | .sig 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN + referrers 200 empty | N/A: push 401 without the server's per-boot credential |
| cluster registry (svc DNS) | dial: connection refused (wrong port) | .sig 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN + referrers 200 empty | N/A: push 401 without the server's per-boot credential |
Positive controls (primary): legacy .sig over the single-platform digest -> present, digest matches; bundle referrer -> present,
DSSE subject matches; index .sig -> present, names the index digest.
The three outcomes are distinct on every transport where they could be produced: a transport error or 5xx; a 404/MANIFEST_UNKNOWN
with an empty referrers list; a fetched, digest-verified payload naming another digest.
